summary: The vault is 1,280,088 pair events from 2026-07-13 to 2026-10-13 (177 coins). Days: 93 calendar days contain events; the engine's annualisation window, which counts whole days from the vault start to the last event day, is 92 days. The model, the pick rule, the 10 h probability calibration and the backtest settings were fixed before any vault label or outcome was read, and nothing in them was changed afterwards. Two deviations are on record: the p_cal pool used folds 0-7 with the guard t0 + 10 h <= vault start (a ruling made after the vault was scored and before any label was read, differing from the brief's wording), and the refit's reproduction check on fold 0 (2a) missed its preset tolerance and was accepted by the user as solver-level agreement (see Known gaps). The 2 h and 5 h calibration maps and this report were added afterwards at the user's request; the maps are fitted on search-period data only.

Ranking: the vault's own top 1% by p_10h has a lift of 0.0621 (interval 0.0359 to 0.0873). The comparator is S1-D's top 1% over folds 0-7 (the search-period out-of-fold predictions), which had 0.0841 (0.0710 to 0.0976). The vault point estimate is below the S1-D figure (over folds 1-7 only, the test months used in the trading tables, the n-weighted value from the same file is 0.0830, no interval available). The vault and S1-D (folds 0-7) intervals overlap, so the difference between the two point estimates is not established by these intervals, and the vault interval is wholly above zero.
Probabilities: for the Rule A q=1% picks the model's raw p_10h averages 0.7973, the calibrated p 0.6617, and the actual reach rate is 0.6836.

Trading: 12 of 24 runs ended above the $1,000 start at max_open 10 and 12 of 24 at max_open 20; in the test months the counts were 18 and 19. The engine window is 92 days for the vault and 202-203 days for the test period, so equity and return are not per-month comparable.
Reference run (q 1%, no stop, maker fees): vault open10 ends at $2,068.41, open20 at $3,357.10; the same runs in the test months ended at $5,034.35 and $16,935.92.
Best vault run at max_open 10: q 1% / no stop / maker fees, $2,068.41; at max_open 20: q 1% / no stop / maker fees, $3,357.10. Worst at max_open 20: q 1% / stop 0.5 sigma / taker fees, $265.02.
Liquidations in the 48 vault runs: 0. Slippage is set to zero, so results are an upper bound.
findings: Concentration by coin: the q=1% picks touch 177 coins; the top 5 coins carry 10.3% of pick legs and the top 10 carry 15.0% (test months: 10.4% and 15.4%).
Direction: 49.5% of the vault q=1% picks short the spread (z > 0) against 49.2% in the test months.
Maker versus taker: runs above $1,000 at max_open 10 are 9 of 12 with maker fees and 3 of 12 with taker fees in the vault (12 and 6 in the test months); at max_open 20: 9 and 3 (12 and 7).
Unseen coins: 24,094 vault events involve coins the model never saw (CASHCAT, PONS, USELESS); 277 of the q=1% picks are among them.

model_known_gaps: pre-vault model reuses fold 7's lam on 1.35x its train rows (summed loss, see s1_newton.py/hazard_logistic.py), so the relative penalty is slightly weaker; same rule as every fold's refit (1.27x, fold 7's own train+val vs train).

2a (fold 0 refit-only reproduction, round 3) FAILED its pre-set tolerance 6.557e-05 (outside it: p_2h 637, p_5h 9,765, p_10h 40,238 of 428,849 fold 0 test events) and was ACCEPTED on the user's explicit yes as solver-level agreement; max |delta p| per horizon: p_2h 0.001748, p_5h 0.002003, p_10h 0.001832. Attributed to the unsaved warm-start intercepts b0 (s1_run.py refit starts b from the selection fit) plus the lasso's non-strict convexity (unproven). Source: research/model/logs/s1/vault_pull/vault-refit_i-095394542d9f95783.log via diagnostics/vault_2a_maxdiff.py.
